title: autotune: add defaults for batching/caching and quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Alex Chen
description: Motivation: reduce unit token cost for common workloads by shipping conservative defaults and UEcon tooling so teams can opt-in to autotuning safely. This PR adds: 1) new default batching and KV-caching heuristics (per-model presets + dynamic warm-up) to the serving runtime so small/medium customers get cost wins without manual tuning; 2) a configurable quantization profile registry with safe defaults (8-bit and mixed-8 variants) and a validation step to estimate quality/regression risk; 3) unit-economics tooling in the console backend and CLI that exposes per-route token cost, projected savings when applying profiles, and an autosuggest action to preview performance vs cost tradeoffs. Checklist: - [x] runtime batching heuristics and config schema - [x] KV cache default thresholds and warm-up policy - [x] quant profile registry + validation step - [x] CLI command redwood uecon preview - [x] backend endpoints and console panel for UEcon recommendations - [x] unit tests and integration tests for common models - [x] docs and changelog entry Non-goals: autoscaling policy changes and model retraining. See ENG-2345 for background and SUP-7821 for customer-reported cost complaints. Runbook: revertable feature flag runtime.autotune_defaults and registry.quantsafe_key for Canary. This description is intentionally concise and continuous to match PR export requirements.

release_notes: Adds autotune defaults for batching and KV caching, introduces safe quantization profiles and a unit-economics preview tool in the console and CLI. Feature gated behind runtime.autotune_defaults and registry.quantsafe_key.
notes: Deployed to canary region on 2026-02-12. Canary metrics showed 12-18% token cost reduction on average for document-summarization workloads with negligible quality regression per validation harness.
